thread:
michaela: Quick follow-up: we need a binding model for delegated API keys crossing org/project boundaries. Specifically: how do we map billing_owner vs enforcement_owner and what defaults should SDKs use for TTLs?

lee: Proposal: billing_owner defaults to operator service (simpler for quotas). enforcement_owner uses origin principal when policy allows. Token includes both fields in metadata.

jordan: Agree on two-owner fields. Add a policy flag `allow_origin_enforcement` per target service. If false, enforcement_owner=billing_owner.

nora: For TTLs: SDK default 10m, max 2h per-service cap. Support requested_ttl negotiation at mint time and return granted_ttl. Also include `refresh_after` in response for client scheduling.

sam: Ops: enforce_token_revocation via existing pubsub. Proxies subscribe and honor urgency. For cross-org tokens, require a signed delegation_proof so downstream can validate without issuer roundtrip.

michaela: How do we avoid metrics cardinality?

jordan: Core metrics only tag billing_owner. origin_id is pseudonymized and only in traces/logs and sampled metrics (0.5% default). Console can show origin in audit view behind permission.

nora: Edge case: cross-org background jobs. Deny automatic extension of delegated tokens. Require explicit escalation with owner consent recorded in audit.

sam: Also add delegation_chain_limit=3 and proof_version=v2 requirement. Sec-bot will enforce issuance checks.

sec-bot: POLICY: delegation_chain_max=3; proof_version=v2 mandatory after 2025-01-01.

michaela: Action items: implement token metadata fields, SDK defaults & jitter for refresh, revocation pubsub hookup, sampled telemetry pipeline, and console audit view guardrails. I'll file follow-up PRs. Thanks all.
